title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages, Longue Marche notes c. 1981). K is a field finitely generated over Q. Σ = Γ_K = Gal(K̄/K). π = Gal(K̄/K·Q̄) is the geometric part. Γ = Gal(Q̄/k), with k = Q̄ ∩ K, is identified with an open subgroup of Γ_Q. This gives an extension 1 → π → Σ → Γ → 1, and hence an outer action φ: Γ → Out(π). The previous page recasts fields K as such 'exterior' extensions (equivalently as topoi B_K over B_Q). The next page states Theorem 2: the functor K ↦ (Π_K → Π_Q) from fields of finite type to profinite groupoids over Π_Q is faithful.

This page ('Remarques', p. 10) strengthens an earlier Theorem 1, which presumably gives trivial centralizers of open subgroups inside π. The claim: when π ≠ 1 (K not finite over Q), every open subgroup π' ⊂ π has trivial centralizer in the whole Σ, i.e. Centr_Σ(π') = {1}.

Proof sketch on the page, with ζ = Centr_Σ(π'):
(i) ζ ∩ π = 1 by Th. 1, so ζ injects into Γ ⊂ Γ_Q.
(ii) It suffices to show the image of ζ in Γ is finite. Then ζ is a finite subgroup of an absolute Galois group in characteristic 0. By Artin–Schreier, ζ has order 1 or 2, and in the second case it is generated by a complex conjugation (an involution of Γ_Q).
(iii) For finiteness, pass to an open subgroup Σ₁ of Σ (a finite extension of K) whose geometric part is π' itself. Then the image ζ' of ζ ∩ Σ₁ in Γ₁ centralizes π', so it lies in the kernel of φ₁: Γ₁ → Out(π').
(iv) Grothendieck asserts φ is injective. He reduces to transcendence degree 1, then to the π₁ of an algebraic curve.

Modern completion of (iv): an element acting by an inner automorphism on π acts by an inner automorphism on every characteristic quotient π₁(U), U open in the curve. One then uses Belyi's theorem (Γ_Q acts faithfully on π₁ of P¹−{0,1,∞}, or of any hyperbolic curve). So ζ ∩ Σ₁ ⊂ π' ⊂ π, hence ζ ∩ Σ₁ = 1 and ζ is finite.

Purpose: this is the 'slimness' (centralizer-freeness) input. It makes the passage from fields to exterior extensions / groupoids over Π_Q rigid, so that 2-morphisms are trivial. That rigidity is needed for the faithfulness statement (Theorem 2) on the next page.
errors: The page stops at 'ζ is of order 1 or 2' and never excludes the order-2 case, which the stated claim Centr_Σ(π') = {1} requires. The gap closes easily. If ζ = ⟨c⟩ with c an involution, then Centr_{Γ_K}(c) = ⟨c⟩: an element commuting with c preserves the real closure R = K̄^c and induces a K-automorphism of it, which is trivial by Artin–Schreier uniqueness. Then π' ⊂ ⟨c⟩, which is impossible since π' is infinite.
Notation slip: 'Γ_{K̄/K} ⊂ Γ_{Q̄/Q}' should denote Gal(Q̄/k), with k the algebraic closure of Q in K, not Gal(K̄/K).
The injectivity of φ is only claimed ('sauf erreur, je sais prouver'). The reduction is sketched, and the curve case is implicitly Belyi-type faithfulness; no proof is written on the page.

ideas.what: Open subgroups of the geometric Galois group π have trivial centralizer in the full arithmetic Galois group Γ_K of a finitely generated field of positive transcendence degree.
ideas.modern_name: Slimness / centralizer-freeness of geometric fundamental groups in arithmetic ones (Mochizuki's 'slim' groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Anabelian literature of the 1990s–2000s (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki; Pop in the birational setting)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the Faltings letter as such; possibly in circulated transcriptions of the Longue Marche notes

ideas.what: Faithfulness of the outer Galois action Γ → Out(π) for function fields, reduced to curves and then to π₁ of a curve.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of the outer Galois representation (Belyi; Matsumoto, Hoshi–Mochizuki for general hyperbolic curves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi 1979 (consequence noted by Grothendieck); Matsumoto 1996 for affine hyperbolic curves; Hoshi–Mochizuki for the general case
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (1984), discussion of Belyi and faithfulness of Γ_Q on the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Using Artin–Schreier to pin down finite subgroups (order ≤2, complex conjugations) of the centralizer.
ideas.modern_name: Artin–Schreier theorem on torsion in absolute Galois groups
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings / Esquisse mention real sections and complex conjugations in the section-conjecture context

ideas.what: Passing to a finite extension of K to reduce from an open π' to the whole π.

missed.claim: Very early (c. 1981) written formulation of the slimness of Γ_K relative to its geometric subgroup for function fields over Q. It is proved via Belyi faithfulness plus Artin–Schreier, and serves as the rigidity input for a birational faithfulness theorem (Theorem 2, next page). It anticipates arguments later standard in Mochizuki/Pop, but the results themselves are now well known.
missed.quote: la théorie peut se renforcer, sauf erreur, en écrivant que pour les sous-groupes π'⊂π ouverts dans π, Centr_Σ(π') = {1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it shows Grothendieck had the 'slim' rigidity mechanism of birational anabelian geometry in hand in 1981. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The statements (trivial centralizers, faithfulness of the outer Galois action via reduction to curves and Belyi) are now standard anabelian facts. The page is mainly of historical interest as an early, slightly incomplete sketch of the slimness argument underlying birational faithfulness.
transcription_corrections: 'ce qui prouvera, dans [?], que' likely reads 'ce qui prouvera déjà, que' ('déjà' is the interlinear insertion).
'conjuguée par un τ de conjugaisons complexes' is more plausibly 'est un des τ de conjugaison complexe', i.e. the image is generated by a complex conjugation.
'la théorie [?] peut' could be 'le théorème peut se renforcer'; the image is ambiguous.
The interlinear insertion is 'i.e. K pas fini sur Q,' (written above the line); the duplicated header line in the machine transcription is spurious.
